items.text: WHYISCALCIUMOXIDECa2+O2-ANDNOTCa+O-?

items.label: text
items.text: You may think that the answer to this question is obvious. You might say that calcium oxide is Ca2+O2- becauseboth ions would then have a stable noble gas electronic configuration.

items.label: text
items.text: If that is what you believe, then the following may come as a surprise.Acquiringanoblegaselectronicconfigurationisnot areasonforelectronicchangestotakeplacewhen atoms and moleculesreacttogether

items.label: text
items.text: After all,manyionsexistinstablecompounds,inparticular, cationsofthetransitionmetals,inwhichtheydonothavethe electronicconfigurationofanoblegas.Infact,compoundsin whichtheionsdohavea noblegaselectronicconfiguration arein the minority.

items.label: text
items.text: So,why does calcium oxide form as Ca2+O²-and not as Ca+O-, and why are we asking the question?

items.label: text
items.text: Youmayrememberthatwehavementionedthattheformationof O-(g)fromO(g)is exothermic:

items.label: formula
items.text: O(g) + e⁻ → O⁻(g)   1st EA = −141 kJ mol⁻¹

items.label: text
items.text: However, the formation of O²-(g) from O(g)is endothermic:

items.label: formula
items.text: O(g) + 2e⁻ → O²⁻(g)   1st EA + 2nd EA = +657 kJ mol⁻¹

items.label: text
items.text: Since more energy is required, why is the formation of the O²- ion preferredovertheformationofO-?

items.label: text
items.text: A similar pattern is observed with the formation of Ca+(g) and Ca²+(g) from Ca(g):

items.label: formula
items.text: Ca(g) → Ca+(g) + e- 1st IE = +590kJ mol-1 Ca(g) → Ca2+(g) + 2e- 1st IE+ 2nd IE= +1735kJ mol-1

items.label: text
items.text: Similarly, since more energy is required, why is the formation of theCa²+ionpreferredovertheformationoftheCa+ion?
